claims.claim: Grown neural networks converge to flatter minima compared to fixed-size models trained from scratch.
Grown neural networks achieve better generalization performance than fixed-size models trained from scratch.

initialization_strategy: random initialization of newly added neurons
mechanistic_notes: Adding neurons modifies the loss landscape, increasing basin width and flattening minima.
Dynamic architecture changes affect gradient flow, promoting exploration of flatter regions.
selection_criterion: growth triggered when training progress stagnates (inferred)
summary: The paper shows that neural networks grown by incrementally adding neurons during training reach flatter minima and generalize better than static networks trained from scratch.
website_alignment_notes: Mechanistic decomposition focuses on how growth operator alters optimization dynamics rather than performance marketing.
